program_name: Bachelor in Informatics and Management of Digital Business (IT: Laurea in Informatica e Management delle Aziende Digitali; DE: Bachelor in Wirtschaftsinformatik). Jointly delivered by the Faculty of Engineering (formerly Faculty of Computer Science) and the Faculty of Economics and Management. Degree course director: Prof. Marco Montali; Faculty of Economics representative: Dr. Paola Rovelli.
level: bachelor (first-cycle degree, 3 years, 180 ECTS). Graduates may sit the Italian State Examination to qualify as 'Ingegnere dell'informazione iunior' and register in Section B of the Italian Register of Engineers.
teaching_language: Trilingual: German, Italian and English are all official teaching languages. Weighting in the published 2026/27 course offering (individual teaching units): 13 units in English, 4 in German, 2 in Italian, plus 2 composite courses split across English and German. English carries most of the first-year core (Introduction to Programming, Economics of Digital Markets, Accounting for Decision Making, Introduction to Linear Algebra and Discrete Mathematics, Introduction to Analysis and Optimization Techniques, Modeling and Databases with Project, Application Engineering for Business Informatics, Engineering of Mobile Systems, Change Management, Digital Finance and Financial Markets). Italian carries Data Structures and Algorithms (6 CP) and Management of System Security and Networks (6 CP). German carries Probability Theory and Statistics (6 CP), Web and Internet Engineering with Project (6 CP), ERP Systems and IT Management (7 CP) and Strategic Management and Digital Business (5 CP). Two dedicated language courses are embedded in the curriculum: 'English for Informatics and Digital Business' (3 CP, year 2) and 'Italian/German for Informatics and Digital Business' (3 CP, year 3). Language mix per course can shift from year to year, so the split above is the 2026/27 snapshot rather than a fixed rule.
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (Faculty of Engineering secretariat: Bruno-Buozzi-Strasse 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy). Not the Bolzano city-centre main campus, and not Brixen-Bressanone or Bruneck-Brunico.
degree_class: L-31 (Scienze e tecnologie informatiche / Computer Science and Technologies). National regulations allow simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes, but the two must not belong to the same class (e.g. L-31 + L-31 is not permitted) and must differ by at least 2/3 of course contents.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and confirmed running. The 2026/27 admission-information PDF (last update 03.08.2026) is published, and both the 2026/27 Early Bird and Late Application ranking lists have already been published, with 40 EU candidates admitted in the Early Bird session and a further 15 EU candidates in the Late Application session. Unlike Wood Technology and Tourism Management, this programme is genuinely open in 2026/27. The course-offering page also already lists a 2027/28 academic year option.
is_new_programme: NO — this is NOT a new programme and 2026/27 is NOT the first intake. The programme was first activated in academic year 2019/20 (Manifesto degli studi, a.a. 2019/20, published 28/02/2019 and 22/07/2019 at /assets/Documents/Study-Manifestos/2019/), and unibz announced its first three graduates on 21 July 2022 — consistent with a 2019/20 first cohort completing a 3-year degree. Course pages exist for academic years 2025 and 2026 and ranking lists exist for 2026/27, further confirming continuous operation. The research brief's note 'new programme — first intake 2026/27' is incorrect and should be corrected in the source dataset. What IS relatively recent is the organisational move: the programme now sits under the Faculty of Engineering (the former Faculty of Computer Science) and is based at the NOI Techpark campus, and the URL still resolves under both /faculties/engineering/ and /faculties/computer-science/.
majors_tracks_study_plans: Two specialisation study plans, both sharing an identical first year and differing by 18 CP of specialisation credits: (1) Specialisation in Digital Finance and Financial Markets — 12 CP second-year course 'Digital Finance and Financial Markets' (Module 1: Principles of Finance for CS, 6 CP; Module 2: Financial Markets, 6 CP) plus a 6 CP third-year elective chosen from 'Current Topics in Digital Finance and Financial Markets' or 'Advanced Economics for Digital Business'. (2) Specialisation in Digital Marketing and Advertising — 12 CP second-year course 'Digital Marketing and Advertising' (Module 1: Introduction to Digital Marketing and Advertising, 6 CP; Module 2: Advanced Topics in Digital Marketing and Advertising, 6 CP) plus a 6 CP third-year elective chosen from 'Advanced Economics for Digital Business' or 'Current Topics in Digital Marketing and Advertising'. Both plans also include 12 CP Free Choice, a compulsory internship (6 CP, minimum 150 hours), a 5 CP Seminar in Business Informatics and Information Systems and a 6 CP Thesis. There is no dual-study or 4-year variant, and the specialisation is not chosen at application time — the application is to the single L-31 programme.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. Admission requires certified B2 in at least TWO of the three teaching languages (German, Italian, English); applicants who cannot prove this are excluded from the admission procedure outright, before any ranking is computed. An applicant who only speaks English can at best certify one language and therefore cannot be admitted. Graduation additionally requires C1 in the 1st language, C1 in the 2nd and B2 in the 3rd, and two core courses are taught only in Italian and four only in German. The published 2026/27 ranking lists quantify the barrier: in the Early Bird session 12 EU applicants and 4 of the 5 non-EU applicants were excluded for failing the language requirements, and 6 more EU applicants were excluded in the Late Application session — a total of 22 language-based exclusions against 55 admissions. For a Turkish candidate this means the realistic path is to certify B2 in English plus B2 in either Italian or German before the application deadline; English-only candidates should be routed instead to unibz's fully English-taught Bachelor in Computer Science.
admission_type: Restricted access / numero programmato with document-based selection — there is NO written entrance exam. The admission type combination is: (a) restricted access with fixed quotas, (b) a language-proficiency eligibility filter (B2 in 2 of the 3 teaching languages) that excludes applicants before ranking, and (c) an Admission Committee evaluation of self-declared secondary-school grades plus certified extracurricular experience, producing a ranking list. There is no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no unibz subject entrance test, no interview and no portfolio for this programme.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): a secondary school leaving certificate from the Italian system, or a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent. Foreign school-leaving certificates count as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND at least the last two years were attended in that foreign school system (unibz explicitly warns that attending one year and obtaining, e.g., the Irish Leaving Certificate is not enough). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific admission requirements for holders of certain certificates (American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named); such candidates should contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Beyond the qualification, applicants must possess: (1) adequate general competence and disciplinary competence in the mathematical area — assessed from the average grade of the third-last and penultimate year of secondary school plus any other documents the commission requests, and (2) adequate knowledge of at least two of the three teaching languages. This is a bachelor programme, so there are no ECTS or SSD credit prerequisites; the 2024 SSD reform codes (e.g. INFO-01/A, IINF-05/A, ECON-04/A, MATH-02/A, MATH-03/A, MATH-03/B, ECON-06/A, ECON-07/A, ECON-09/A, ECON-09/B, GIUR-01/A, ANGL-01/C) appear in this programme only as the classification of its own taught courses, not as entry requirements.
entry_exam_or_test: No entrance examination of any kind is required for admission — neither the unibz subject test, nor TOLC-I, nor CENT-S. Selection is purely document-based.

unibz Language Centre language proficiency exams (optional route to prove B2, only if the applicant cannot document proficiency another way). Online. Early Bird dates: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026). Late Application dates: 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Only B2-level exams can be registered for.

Post-admission only, not part of selection: the OFA mathematics catch-up test, taken after the Faculty's catch-up course and before the 'Introduction to Linear Algebra and Discrete Mathematics' course, for candidates whose mathematics average was at or below 65% of the maximum grade.

Post-admission only, not part of selection: a third-language placement test for admitted students who could not certify their third teaching language; the result assigns them to a learning path towards B2.
selection_scoring: The Admission Committee awards a maximum of 11 points in total: up to 4 points for the average of all grades; up to 6 points for the grade average in mathematics; up to 1 point overall for proven extracurricular experiences in economic/IT areas. Grades from the third-last and penultimate year of secondary school are used. In case of a tie, preference goes to the younger applicant. No minimum passing score or grade threshold is published — the programme is ranked, not threshold-gated, and the effective cut-off is simply the number of available places. In practice the ranking barely binds: in the Early Bird 2026/27 session 41 eligible EU candidates competed for 40 places, so only one candidate went onto the waiting list, and only 1 non-EU candidate was admitted against 4 reserved places. The real filter is the language requirement, not the score. A separate scoring consequence: candidates scoring at or below 65% of the maximum grade on the mathematics average receive OFA (additional learning obligations) — 16 of the 40 admitted EU candidates in the Early Bird 2026/27 list carry an OFA marker.
bonus_points: No Webometrics university-ranking bonus, no GMAT/GRE bonus and no startup/project-pitch bonus apply to this programme — those mechanisms belong to unibz master programmes (Software Engineering, Computing for Data Science, Accounting and Finance, Entrepreneurship). The only bonus-like element here is the extracurricular component: up to 1 point overall for proven extracurricular experiences in the economic/IT field, declared on a provided self-declaration form for a maximum of 2 experiences. Examples given by unibz: participation in robotics competitions, mathematics olympiads, computer competitions, and online courses with certificate. For each experience a contact person must be indicated so unibz can verify it.
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no video, no project proposal and no motivation letter are required or accepted for this programme — none of unibz's format limits (20 MB portfolio PDF, 2 A4 project proposal, 6,000-character motivation letter, 2-minute video) apply here. The structured materials that must be produced in the application portal instead are: (1) self-declaration of the subjects and grades of the third-last and penultimate secondary school years; (2) if those years were completed abroad, uploaded copies of the relevant school report cards; (3) unibz's provided self-declaration form for up to a maximum of 2 certified extracurricular experiences in the economic/IT field, each naming a contact person for verification; (4) official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optional upload of language certificates under the corresponding menu point. There is no study-career Excel template for this bachelor (that requirement belongs to master applications).
interview: No interview. Selection is entirely document-based and no interview dates are published for this programme in any of the three 2026/27 application sessions.
conditional_admission: Applicants who have not yet obtained their secondary school diploma may apply — this is the normal case for final-year school pupils. If the diploma is not yet held at application time, it must be uploaded at enrolment; the qualification diploma is a mandatory enrolment document for foreign qualifications. If a candidate pays the first instalment but then fails the final secondary school exam, the fees are refundable (the general no-refund rule is explicitly waived for that case, and for non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the necessary documents from the Italian authorities in their country). Non-EU citizens living abroad are admitted 'with reserve' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt): the reserve is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. If a candidate does not possess a valid admission qualification, unibz can exclude them by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The ECTS-based conditional admission rules (>=120 ECTS, 140 for Data Analytics) and the 11/12/2026 late-enrolment fallback belong to master programmes and do not apply to this bachelor.
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) in the mathematics area are assigned during the admission procedure to any admitted candidate whose mathematics grade average is equal to or lower than 65% of the maximum grade. There is no separate compulsory mathematics test at application time — the OFA decision is made from the school grades. A student with OFA must attend the Faculty's catch-up mathematics course before the 'Introduction to Linear Algebra and Discrete Mathematics' course starts and pass the relevant test. If the test is failed, the student follows an individual study programme agreed with a tutor and must still clear the OFA within the first year, either by passing the test or by passing the 'Introduction to Linear Algebra and Discrete Mathematics' exam. If the OFA is not cleared within the first year the student may enrol in the second year but cannot sit any second- or third-year exams. Frequency in practice: 16 of the 40 EU candidates admitted in the Early Bird 2026/27 ranking list, and 4 of the 15 admitted in the Late Application list, are flagged with OFA.
language_requirements: This is the decisive field for this programme. The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and applicants must certify B2 in at least two of them or be excluded from the admission procedure. Entry: 1st language B2, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required. Exit (to graduate): 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2, all on the Common European Framework of Reference. The 'first' language is defined as the one in which the applicant is strongest, the 'third' as the weakest or a complete beginner language — the positions are assigned by proficiency, not by which specific language it is. Certification is mandatory for the first and second language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the third. Only B2-level exams can be booked at the unibz Language Centre. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum needed to take curricular examinations in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is the applicant's third language, at least B1 in English must be certified by mid-January to be able to sit all first-semester curricular exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2; absolute beginners must use the September intensive course because A1 beginner courses are offered exclusively in the September pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year. Certificates issued by an Italian public institution are declared via self-declaration; those from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scanned copy of the original. If a foreign or bi-/multilingual school diploma explicitly states CEFR levels (B1, B2 or C1) for German, Italian or English AND all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the second and/or third language, subject to Language Centre approval.
entry_levels_by_position: B2 / B2 / no level required (1st / 2nd / 3rd language position). Positions are assigned by proficiency, not by language: the 1st language is whichever of German, Italian or English the applicant is strongest in, the 3rd is the weakest. Certification is compulsory for positions 1 and 2 and recommended (B1+) for position 3. Practical consequence for international candidates: English alone satisfies only one of the two required positions, so a second B2 in German or Italian is mandatory at application time. Only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre, so the 1st-language requirement is also satisfied by a B2 pass — no C1 is needed to enter.
exit_levels: C1 (1st language) / C1 (2nd language) / B2 (3rd language). These are graduation requirements, so a student admitted with B2/B2 must raise both to C1 and bring the third language from zero to B2 during the three years in order to graduate. Language Centre courses are free of charge and structured to deliver B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language. Special case explicitly flagged by unibz: if the first semester of the programme is taught only in English and English is the student's third language, at least B1 in English must be certified by mid-January in order to sit all first-semester curricular exams. Admitted students who cannot certify their third language take a placement test (details sent by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path towards B2.
proof_pathways: Four accepted pathways: (1) the main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter/document from the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload their obtained certificates and/or declare passed unibz Language Centre exams (B2, B2+ or C1); for foreign degrees, a letter from the university stating the medium of instruction must be added if unclear. (3) A recognised language certificate from unibz's official list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent as a PDF by e-mail or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked online through the application portal ('enrol for language exams') after creating an application. 2026/27 exam dates (all online): 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026) for the Early Bird session; 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026) for the Late Application session. No Language Centre exam session is listed for the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026), so applicants in that session must already hold acceptable proof. If an application is started outside a registration window, the applicant must return to the portal during one of the windows to register. A fifth partial route: a foreign or bi-/multilingual school diploma that explicitly states CEFR levels with all four skills assessed can be accepted for the 2nd and/or 3rd language.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 (Delibera del Consiglio dell'Universita n. 16/2026 / Beschluss des Universitatsrates 16/2026). Rules: international certificates must not be older than 5 years at the date of submission, with the whole calendar year counting from 1 January of the fifth year; the certificate must assess all four skills (reading, writing, listening, speaking) and must be issued by the certification organisation itself; if no overall result/level is stated on the certificate, the LOWEST level reached in any sub-skill determines the recognised level — there is no compensation between skills; certificates obtained as remote/online 'home edition' exams are NOT recognised, except for the specific ones explicitly marked as such in unibz's list (some IELTS variants carry the 'also accepted as home edition' marker); attestations issued by individual lecturers, readers or language teachers are not recognised; DAAD certificates are not recognised. Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' (e.g. certain school diplomas and bilingualism certificates) have unlimited validity rather than the 5-year limit.
application_deadline_eu: Three separate sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment, all closing at noon local time. (1) Early Bird Application: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. (2) Late Application (EU only): 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. (3) Additional Application Session (EU only, opened by the Faculty only if places remain): 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. Applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and a candidate excluded in the first session may apply again in the second. Source wording: 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)'; 'Application: 28/05 - 08/07/2026 (by noon local time)'; 'Application: 18/08 - 04/09/2026 (by noon local time)'.
application_deadline_non_eu: Single window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (by noon local time), the Early Bird Application. Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have no Late Application and no Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 administration fee applies. This is the binding date for Turkish candidates resident in Turkey, and it falls roughly 6 months before classes start on 2026-09-28.
parity_of_treatment: Treated as EU citizens (50 places, three sessions, no application fee): (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay (permesso di soggiorno) under article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, or religious reasons. Critical caveat for Turkish and other non-EU applicants: a permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a tourist visa is NOT sufficient. The permit copy must be uploaded in the application portal; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. If the permit is not uploaded, the applicant is automatically reclassified as a non-EU citizen living abroad and must go through the Italian consular admission procedure with the single Early Bird window and the 4-place quota. A Turkish citizen resident in Turkey therefore falls into the non-EU-abroad category; a Turkish citizen already in Italy on a family or work permit falls into the parity category.
places_quotas: Three separate numbers for 2026/27: EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — Early Bird Application 40 places, Late Application 10 places (50 EU places in total); non-EU citizens living abroad — Early Bird Application 4 places (no Late or Additional session). Any places left unfilled from the EU Early Bird round roll over into the Late Application round, which is why the published Late Application ranking list admitted 15 candidates against a nominal 10 places. Actual 2026/27 outcome from the published ranking lists: Early Bird admitted 40 EU candidates with exactly 1 candidate (position 41) on the waiting list, and admitted just 1 non-EU candidate out of the 4 reserved places (4 of the 5 non-EU applicants were excluded for failing the language requirements); Late Application admitted 15 EU candidates. Total admitted across both published sessions: 55 EU + 1 non-EU. The non-EU quota is therefore under-subscribed rather than competitive — the constraint is the language bar, not the number of seats.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking lists published by 2026-05-27; payment of the 1st instalment of the tuition fees to secure the place by 2026-06-05 at noon; enrolment from 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 at noon; waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 2026-06-06 if admitted candidates fail to secure their place in time. Late Application: ranking lists published by 2026-07-30; 1st instalment by 2026-08-06 at noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 at noon. Additional Application Session: ranking lists published by 2026-09-18; 1st instalment by 2026-09-25 at noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-09-25 at noon. Missing the payment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next candidate on the ranking list is admitted; missing the enrolment deadline has the same effect. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the designated rate twice. Paying does not confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund for paying without enrolling, except where the candidate fails the secondary school final exam or (for non-EU applicants abroad) fails to obtain the necessary documents from the Italian authorities. Ranking lists are published at unibz.it/en/applicants/ranking-lists and are valid only for the respective academic year.
programme_specific_dates: There is no programme-specific entrance exam, interview or portfolio deadline for this programme — its only programme-specific dated events are the language exam windows and the academic calendar. Language exams (online, unibz Language Centre): 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09) and 2026-04-16/17 and 2026-04-20/21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08) for the Early Bird session; 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15) for the Late Application session. Pre-semester: intensive language courses 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-18 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day); pre-courses 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09; Freshers Days 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29. 1st semester: classes 2026-09-28 to 2026-12-23, holidays 2026-12-24 to 2027-01-06, classes resume 2027-01-07 to 2027-01-23, exams 2027-01-25 to 2027-02-20. 2nd semester: classes 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-25, holidays 2027-03-26 to 2027-03-29, classes 2027-03-30 to 2027-06-12, exams 2027-06-14 to 2027-07-10. Autumn exam session: 2027-08-23 to 2027-09-25. Note the OFA catch-up mathematics course runs before the 'Introduction to Linear Algebra and Discrete Mathematics' course, i.e. within the September pre-course window.
required_documents: At application (uploaded in the online Application Portal): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document results in exclusion from the admission procedure; the completed online application form; self-declared subjects and grades for the third-last and penultimate secondary school years; copies of the relevant school report cards if those years were completed abroad; official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; unibz's provided self-declaration form for up to 2 certified extracurricular experiences in the economic/IT field, each with a named contact person for verification; language certificates (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd), uploaded under 'upload language certificates' — self-declaration if issued by an Italian public institution, scanned copy of the original if issued by a foreign public institution; the qualification diploma if already obtained abroad (otherwise uploaded at enrolment); for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid permesso di soggiorno (plus renewal request if expired). At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload: the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English); and the recognition documents described under credential_recognition. There is no study-career Excel template for this bachelor programme. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list.
application_fee: EUR 50, charged ONLY to non-EU citizens living abroad. It is an administration fee and is non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay no application fee. Source wording: 'Application fee: EUR 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.'
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ — Fees amount to approximately EUR 1,200 per year, paid in two instalments: the 1st instalment of EUR 600 (which includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp) secures the admitted place and is due by the session's payment deadline; the 2nd instalment of EUR 600 must be paid by March of the following year. Payment is made with a pagoPA payment slip after an e-mail invitation from the Student Office. Late payment of the 2nd instalment triggers a fine (EUR 30) and blocks the online account, preventing exam registration and transfers. From the second year as 'fuori corso' (beyond the normal programme length) a EUR 300 surcharge applies. No reimbursement if the student drops out, interrupts studies or is excluded. Full exemption: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more (certificate from the health authorities to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students receiving a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees.
scholarships_grants: Main instrument: the study grant of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, applied for through the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario (ASUS), worth between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year depending on income; recipients also get their unibz tuition fees refunded. Eligibility barrier for non-EU students: they can apply only if they hold a long-term residence permit OR after at least one uninterrupted year of registered residence in South Tyrol — so a newly arrived Turkish or other non-EU first-year student is effectively unable to access it in year 1 and must budget the full cost of the first year. Other routes: foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship are exempt from tuition fees; unibz merit-based awards and Faculty scholarships exist at university level. No scholarship specific to the Bachelor in Informatics and Management of Digital Business is documented on the programme page or in the 2026/27 admission-information PDF. [uncertain]
credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database - Italy); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence); (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Turkey is a signatory to the Lisbon Convention, so Turkish applicants fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification, with an Italian translation of the diploma unless it is issued in German or English. [uncertain — the Lisbon Convention classification of Turkey is inferred from the convention's signatory list rather than stated on the unibz page, so applicants should confirm with apply@unibz.it.] unibz performs its own checks on foreign qualifications and reserves the right to request additional documents; a candidate without a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The 180-ECTS proof requirement mentioned in the field schema applies to master admissions, not to this bachelor.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window (2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, noon) paying the EUR 50 fee; check the ranking list (published by 2026-05-27); if admitted, secure the place by paying the 1st instalment by 2026-06-05 noon; then start the visa application on the Universitaly portal — this pre-enrolment is MANDATORY, without it enrolment is not allowed, and only ONE study programme can be selected on Universitaly. Non-EU candidates are admitted with reserve until the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. The Italian authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. unibz notes that applying at unibz does not guarantee an appointment at the Italian diplomatic-consular representation. Financial means for the visa: at least EUR 800 per month for living costs in the Bozen-Bolzano area excluding tuition, with unibz estimating a bachelor programme will cost at least EUR 36,000 in total (a master programme EUR 24,000); health insurance and visa expenses come on top. After arrival in Italy the residence permit must be applied for within 8 working days (cost approximately EUR 186.46 in stamp, postal fees and issuance); the applicant should contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival, and the permesso di soggiorno must then be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Health cover is required for the permit: private insurance (e.g. Welcome Association Italy, about EUR 81 for 6 months or EUR 130 for 12 months) or voluntary registration with the Italian National Health Service at about EUR 700 per calendar year. Work with a study residence permit is capped at 20 hours per week and 1,040 hours per year. Permit renewal must be requested at least 60 days before expiry; the first renewal requires at least one passed exam and subsequent renewals two exams per year; study permits can run up to 6 years for a bachelor.

uncertainty_notes: 1) MAJOR CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF: the input record described this as a 'new programme — first intake 2026/27'. That is wrong. The programme has run since academic year 2019/20 (2019 Manifesto degli studi in IT/DE/EN) and produced its first graduates in July 2022, with published course offerings for 2025/26 and 2026/27 and published 2026/27 ranking lists. The dataset entry should be corrected. What changed recently is only the faculty/campus framing (Faculty of Computer Science absorbed into the Faculty of Engineering; NOI Techpark campus). 2) The input record also listed teaching_language as 'trilingual (IT/DE/EN)', which is correct in principle, but the practical mix is heavily English-weighted in the taught courses while the ADMISSION rule still demands B2 in two of the three languages — these two facts must be presented together or the programme will look more accessible than it is. 3) The per-course language split (13 EN / 4 DE / 2 IT / 2 mixed) is the 2026/27 course-offering snapshot from the programme's own course-offering page; unibz warns that page 'does not illustrate the structure of the study programme' and language assignments can change between years, so it is indicative rather than contractual. 4) The maximum total selection score of 11 points is a sum of the three published components (4 + 6 + 1); unibz does not print a total anywhere, and no minimum passing threshold is published at all. 5) No 2026/27 Manifesto degli studi PDF could be found for this programme; official_call_url therefore points to the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, which is the binding published call. 6) Turkey's classification under the Lisbon Convention (case b: ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from the convention's signatory list rather than stated on the unibz page — confirm with apply@unibz.it before advising a candidate. 7) No programme-specific scholarship was found; only the general provincial and university-level instruments are documented. 8) Non-EU visa cost figures (EUR 186.46 residence permit, EUR 81/130 private insurance, EUR 700 SSN) come from the unibz Study Guide and are indicative amounts that change annually. 9) All dates in the sources are written in DD/MM/YYYY and have been normalised to ISO here; the 2026/27 admission-information PDF carries the note 'Subject to change. Latest update: 03.08.2026', and quotas and dates are re-issued every admission cycle. 10) Beware of cached ?v= query strings on the CoursesPDF URLs — search engines surface older academic-year versions (e.g. ?v=96 returning 2025/26 content) at the same base path; always fetch the base URL without a version parameter.
